As AI changes what people and organizations can accomplish, we’re exploring how roles, teams, and ways of working should evolve and putting those ideas into practice within OpenAI. About the role We’re looking for an Organizational Design Lead to help build our organizational design capability and shape how people and AI agents work together. You’ll partner with leaders and People colleagues to understand business goals, examine how work gets done, and design the roles, structures, decision processes, and workflows that help teams succeed. This includes exploring where AI can expand people’s capabilities, how responsibilities should evolve, and where human judgment and accountability are essential. This is a hands-on role. You’ll move between understanding organizational challenges, developing new approaches, testing them with teams, and turning what works into practical tools and methods others can use. You’ll bring a thoughtful perspective on organizations and the ability to make change happen. In this role, you will: - Translate business goals into organizational choices. Help leaders identify the work, capabilities, roles, and team structures needed to achieve their goals. - Design how people and AI agents work together. We then partner closely with Product, Engineering, Research, Comms, and Design teams to create a cohesive customer experience across all our channels. Our focus extends beyond just promoting product features; we aim to provide valuable insights and resources that help our users make the most out of AI technologies. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), Cyber - Tokyo
jobs.description_text: About the Team OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team builds with customers to bring frontier AI into production. Our Cyber FDEs partner with the security and engineering teams that defend globally critical systems, from enterprise software to the core infrastructure it runs on. Cyber FDEs work closely with our Product, Research, and Go-to-Market teams to adapt our products and models to what customers need to defend their systems. About the Role You’ll build systems that give defenders an advantage at a scale few engineering teams encounter. You might help an enterprise identify, test, and deploy patches across hundreds of thousands of code repositories, or help a security team analyze petabytes of logs for signs of malicious agents or coordinated attacks. Across these deployments, you’ll build tools that customer engineers can trust to support consequential security decisions. You’ll work directly with customer security teams, from CISOs to frontline analysts. As AI changes how attackers operate, you’ll help these teams determine where their defenses need to evolve, prioritize what to build, and validate solutions with the engineers who will operate them. Alongside OpenAI’s account teams, you’ll translate security priorities into deployed systems that help defenders cover more ground. You’ll also help shape what OpenAI builds next. We help ensure that the people and organizations using OpenAI are legitimate, that access is used appropriately, and that bad actors are prevented from exploiting our platform. We operate at the intersection of fraud prevention, identity, access, compliance, and abuse detection. Our team partners closely with Product, Engineering, Legal, Go-To-Market, Support, and Security to identify emerging threats, investigate suspicious behavior, and build durable controls that protect OpenAI’s users, revenue, and reputation across all of Open. ABOUT THE ROLE — RISK AND FRAUD ANALYST We’re hiring a Risk and Fraud Analyst to help safeguard OpenAI by investigating, validating, and monitoring customer accounts and organizations. You will focus on identity, legitimacy, and risk, ensuring accounts are properly verified, access is appropriate, and emerging threats are detected early. You’ll handle sensitive and high-stakes investigations involving fraud and scams, impersonation, sanctions, misuse of access, and coordinated abuse. Your work will directly influence who can use OpenAI’s products and how safely we can scale. Note: This role may involve reviewing sensitive, confidential, or disturbing content. jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Robotics Embedded Systems
jobs.description_text: About the Team OpenAI’s Robotics team builds hardware and software for general-purpose robots. We work closely with AI researchers and use what we learn from testing on physical robots to guide the next design. About the Role We’re hiring an Engineering Manager to lead engineers working on firmware, low-level controls, and systems software for onboard compute. You’ll develop the people doing this work and shape the roadmap with technical leads and partners in hardware and research. You’ll stay close enough to the engineering to help the team make difficult calls, whether that means running one more experiment on the bench or deciding that a change is ready to ship. In this role, you will: - Hire and coach engineers, give them clear feedback, and help them grow. Give experienced engineers room to lead designs and create opportunities for others to take on technical ownership. - Set priorities with technical leads and partners in hardware and research. Decide how to staff the work, communicate tradeoffs early, and resolve dependencies that could hold up a hardware milestone. - Guide work on embedded systems, from board bring-up and device interfaces to actuator control. Invest in reusable systems software so other engineers can integrate hardware, command it, and understand how it responds. - Set the bar for changes that ship to physical robots. Use design reviews, hardware-in-the-loop tests, and measurements of timing, tracking accuracy, and fault recovery to judge readiness.

jobs.description_text: The Problem We’re Solving: A home’s survival in a wildfire or flood depends on its materials, geometry, topography, and defensible space. Traditional insurance models flatten that complexity, offering little insight to homeowners and few incentives for mitigation. Stand combines deterministic catastrophe models with modern AI to compute property-level risk and embed it directly into underwriting, pricing, and mitigation workflows. Instead of obscuring risk behind averages, we make it measurable and actionable - giving insurers sharper pricing signals and homeowners clear insight and incentives to mitigate. We build production software that connects scientific modeling to real-world insurance operations, turning physics into decisions. The Role: We’re hiring a Member of the Technical Staff - Product Engineer with engineering excellence - someone who has owned large product surfaces, navigated tradeoffs, and is comfortable being accountable for outcomes, not just implementations. This role is not narrowly scoped. You’ll own critical systems across the insurance lifecycle, from core workflows (policy, underwriting, claims, payments) to entirely new products like wildfire preparedness inspections, risk monitoring, and customer-facing mitigation tools. Python developers reach Supabase from backend services, data pipelines, notebooks, and a growing number of AI agents and agent frameworks. The Python SDK is how all of them talk to the platform: database queries, auth, storage, realtime and edge functions, in both sync and async flavors. This is a library-authoring role, and the work happens in the open: public repos, public issue trackers, and API decisions whose consequences last for years. If you get satisfaction from a type checker that catches the bug before your users do, from an async client that cleans up after itself, and from an issue tracker that isn't a graveyard, you'll like it here. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that scale to millions. WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR - Build and evolve our Python SDK across database, auth, storage, realtime and functions, with both sync and async APIs that feel natural in Python. - Start new things. jobs.title: Engineering Productivity Engineer
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for an EngProd Engineer to join our Engineering Operations team and own the engineering experience from local setup to production deploy. You’ll build and integrate the tools our engineers rely on every day: local development, code search, testing, code review, CI, AI-assisted workflows, and the metrics that show where time is being lost. You’ll work closely with other engineering teams at Supabase to eliminate friction, optimize cycle times, and make reliably shipping to production effortless. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in async, fast-paced environments and is excited about building developer tools that engineers love and that empower them to do their best work. WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR In this role, you’ll: - Improve local development and the daily workflow - Own local development environment stability; eliminate “works on my machine,” keep environments reproducible across teams, and make onboarding and setup self-service for every engineer - Improve the daily editing experience, including IDE and editor tooling, extensions, and code search, indexing, and navigation that stays fast as the codebase grows - Build paved roads: project scaffolding, templates, and golden-path workflows that make the right thing the easy thing - Speed up build, test, and CI - Improve our testing tooling and make sure it works well for engineers, including test orchestration, ephemeral end-to-end environments, and techniques like mutation and chao

jobs.title: FinOps Data Engineer
jobs.description_text: About the Role We're looking for a FinOps Data Engineer to help drive cost optimization and cloud financial governance across our AWS infrastructure and GCP footprint. You'll work cross-functionally with Engineering, Finance, and Product to find and ship savings, build the tooling necessary to maximize efficiency of every dollar spent in the cloud, and cultivate a culture of cost awareness across engineering teams. This role owns the data side of that mission: the models, pipelines, and analysis that make cost, usage, and margin numbers trustworthy across the company. This is a hands-on engineering role, not an analyst seat. You'll do the schlep work other teams don't have time for, digging into a bucket's access pattern, writing the dbt model or Python pipeline that ships the fix, building the cost-vs-revenue mart that answers a margin question once instead of every time, and chasing a number until it reconciles. Strong communication matters as much as technical depth, you'll regularly explain a savings case or a data model's implications to an engineering team, a finance stakeholder, and a leadership audience in the same week. What You'll Be Responsible For In this role, you'll: - Find and ship savings across AWS and GCP: Analyze billing, usage, and cost trends to identify opportunities, rightsizing, storage lifecycle policies, data transfer, and spot/auto-scaling. jobs.title: Engineering Manager - Spark
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead engineering effort on Supabase Spark. Supabase Spark is an initiative to build the next frontier of agentic databases, supporting billions of databases, with millions of databases created every day. Although we don’t require managers to contribute to code directly, we do expect you to participate in design discussions and to be involved in setting the bar for engineering quality and best practices. WHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR Team & People - Build a healthy, high-trust team culture in a remote-first, globally distributed environment. - Run 1:1s, performance management, career development, and onboarding for your direct reports. - Handle people admin (leave, time off, etc.) for your team. Hiring - Own the hiring plan for your team and act as Hiring Manager. First round of interviewer for all roles on the team. - Partner with Talent Acquisition to source, interview, and close strong candidates. - Contribute to headcount planning, org design, and the evolution of engineering leadership at Supabase. Delivery & Roadmap - Own the team's roadmap and project management (Linear), driving accountability and clear milestones. - Manage workflow intake and Slack triage. These are the team’s primary inboxes for cross-team requests. You decide what gets routed where, prioritized, or pushed back on. - Own the team's weekly updates and keep stakeholders aligned without creating overhead. - Organize effort against support ticke
